usageNotes: Use this to inspect the CIDR entries inside a specific cluster-level firewall IPSet by name. Requires Sys.Audit on the root path (/). Each entry includes a cidr, optional comment, a digest (useful for passing to update/delete calls to guard against concurrent edits), and an optional nomatch flag that negates the entry (i.e., excludes that CIDR from the set).

examples.summary: List all CIDRs in an IPSet named 'trusted-mgmt'

tips: The nomatch field, when true, means the CIDR is excluded from the set rather than included — useful for carving exceptions out of a broader range.
Capture the digest from each entry before calling an update or delete; passing it back prevents overwriting concurrent changes.
IPSet names must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores (2–64 chars).
